General administrative complaints · Nigerian complaint guidance

Complaints about public-service delays and administrative unfairness

Prepare a focused complaint about an unexplained administrative delay, refused service, missing decision or other public-service problem in Nigeria.

By PetitionDesk Editorial Team · Reviewed 25 August 2026

Who this guide is for: People affected by an unexplained delay, missing public record, refusal to process an application or other administrative service problem.

Understand the problem before writing

An administrative complaint should identify the public institution, office, application or service involved. State what was requested, when the request was made, what documents were provided and how the institution responded. A clear timeline is usually more persuasive than a general accusation that an entire agency is corrupt or inefficient.

Differentiate a delay from a formal refusal, an incomplete application, a missing payment or a dispute over an eligibility decision. Each situation requires a different remedy. If the office has asked for a document, explain whether it was supplied and provide the relevant reference.

Where a public-service decision affects employment, benefits, identity documents, licensing or access to records, preserve the notice and identify the unit responsible. Do not assume that an unrelated regulator or criminal-enforcement body can direct the agency to issue the outcome you prefer.

Complaint institutions and service-delivery oversight bodies can be relevant when the responsible office does not provide a clear answer. Their usefulness depends on being able to identify the original application, the responsible institution and the practical administrative remedy requested.

Build an evidence checklist

Use records that relate directly to your complaint. Put events in date order, identify the organisation involved, and keep copies of every message or acknowledgement. Describe what your documents actually show; do not present an allegation as a proven finding.

  • Public institution, department and office location
  • Application, case or service reference
  • Submission date and documents provided
  • Copies of receipts, acknowledgement and official responses
  • The practical effect of the delay or disputed decision
  • A clear request for action, explanation or review

Choose the institution that can respond

Start with the office that controls the public-service decision and use an official complaints or enquiries channel. Request an acknowledgement or reference and identify whether you want a status update, a reasoned decision, correction of a record or review of an administrative action.

A company mentioned in a statement, address, receipt or background document is not automatically the institution responsible for the complaint. Identify who provided the disputed service, who made the decision, and who can supply records or correct the problem.

Decide whether escalation is justified

If the responsible institution does not address the issue, a relevant public complaints or service-delivery authority may be appropriate. Include the original application, correspondence and outstanding question rather than copying unrelated agencies.

Before escalating, keep the original complaint reference, the institution's written answer where available, and a concise explanation of what remains unresolved. Check the current instructions published by the relevant authority instead of assuming that one deadline applies to every type of complaint.

Worked example: applying the route in practice

If an application remains unanswered after repeated visits, provide the application reference, submission date, office contacted, documents supplied and the specific request for a written decision or status update.

Avoid common mistakes and protect personal data

Do not demand that an oversight body override an independent court, issue a document outside its mandate or treat an incomplete application as evidence of intentional misconduct without supporting facts.

Remove passwords, one-time passcodes, card security codes and unrelated medical, financial or family information. Request a specific remedy supported by your evidence, such as an explanation, correction, investigation, refund or written decision.

Frequently asked questions

What makes a public-service complaint actionable?

Identify the responsible office, application reference, dated events, prior correspondence and the specific administrative response you are requesting.

Should every delayed application be reported as corruption?

No. Describe the delay and any verifiable irregularity separately. An allegation of corruption needs a factual basis and the correct reporting channel.

Official sources and contact starting points

These links point to the organisations' published websites or complaint resources. Check that the channel and procedure remain current before sharing your complaint or evidence.
